task_context.reference_solution: For the function to be continuous, both of the two expressions must have the same value when $x=3$. Therefore, $3+2=2(3)+a$. Solving, we get that $a=\boxed{-1}$.

If you look at the boundary point $x=3$, the function is continuous if the limit from the left equals the limit from the right. In simpler terms, both expressions must result in the same value when you plug in the boundary value.
Fine. So I should just put 3 into $x+2$ and also put 3 into $2x+a$, and then make those two things equal to each other?

That is exactly the right method. By setting those two expressions equal to each other at the boundary point, you will create a linear equation where $a$ is the only unknown. Once you have that equation, you can solve for $a$.
Okay, I did that. $3+2 = 2(3)+a$, so $5 = 6+a$. That means $a = -1$. Can you just tell me if that's right? I'm almost out of time!
